text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"SQLite has three checkpoint subtypes: PASSIVE, FULL and RESTART.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [5] explicitly lists exactly three checkpoint subtypes: PASSIVE, FULL, and RESTART.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"There are three subtypes of checkpoints that vary in their aggressiveness: PASSIVE, FULL, and RESTART."}]},{"claim_text":"Every checkpoint started with sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() or by the automatic mechanism is PASSIVE.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [5] states that all checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE."}]},{"claim_text":"Calling sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() always produces a FULL or RESTART checkpoint.","verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passages say FULL and RESTART checkpoints can only be initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2(), but they do not say that every call to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() always produces a FULL or RESTART checkpoint.","citations":[]},{"claim_text":"A PASSIVE checkpoint is guaranteed to run to completion as long as no other connection is writing.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage [5] says PASSIVE checkpoints might not run to completion if there are concurrent readers or writers, so absence of writers alone does not guarantee completion.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"The default checkpoint style is PASSIVE, which does as much work as it can without interfering with other database connections, and which might not run to completion if there are concurrent readers or writers."}]},{"claim_text":"A checkpoint can only reset the WAL when no other connection is using it.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [7] states that a checkpoint is only able to run to completion and reset the WAL file if no other database connections are using the WAL file.","citations":[{"index":7,"quote":"A checkpoint is only able to run to completion, and reset the WAL file, if there are no other database connections using the WAL file."}]},{"claim_text":"A checkpoint will always reset the WAL whenever the WAL is unused.","verdict":"UNSUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passages state that no other connections using the WAL is necessary for a checkpoint to reset the WAL, but they do not state that an unused WAL is sufficient to guarantee that a checkpoint will always reset it.","citations":[]},{"claim_text":"The automatic checkpoint is implemented on top of sqlite3_wal_hook().","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [4] states that the automatic checkpoint mechanism is implemented as a simple wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook().","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"The automatic checkpoint mechanism is implemented as a simple wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook()."}]},{"claim_text":"The automatic checkpoint runs in the same thread as the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [3] states that, by default, the checkpoint is run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit."}]},{"claim_text":"Long-running readers never delay the automatic checkpoint.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage [2] states that a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress, and passage [1] explains that a checkpoint must stop at a page past the end mark of any current reader.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"Thus a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress."},{"index":1,"quote":"A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader."}]}]}
